md_description: This workflow covers collection of urban air samples across locations, heights, times, and weather conditions; measurement of environmental context including temperature, humidity, and particulate matter; nucleic acid extraction from collected air material; sequencing-based metagenomic readout; and downstream computational analysis linking airborne microbial community structure to urban environmental and pollution-related factors.

urban_air_sample.reasoning: For the Entity node urban_air_sample, I included only intrinsic sample identity and provenance fields: where, when, and under what ambient collection context the air sample was physically collected. I excluded downstream process details such as extraction, sequencing, filtering, and analysis because those belong to Process/Capture/Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating any environmental measurement values that are explicitly handled by the air_environment_capture node and its raw signal; instead I kept only collection-context descriptors on the sample itself. No fields were already_generated, so there was no need to suppress overlap with prior schema items, but I still avoided future duplication with capture/signal territory by keeping weather context categorical and not adding instrument or file-related properties.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the physically collected urban air sample; use a stable string format such as UA-001 or siteA_h10_t03. This identifier is assigned at collection and links the sample to all downstream extraction and sequencing records.

Identifier for the urban location where the air sample was collected; use a stable site code such as downtown_park_02 or rooftop_central_01. Record at the sampling point, before any processing or measurement steps.

Height above ground level at which the air sample was physically collected, in meters. Typical urban sampling heights may range from 0.5 to 50 m depending on the protocol; record the actual collection height at the sampling point.

Date and time when the air sample was collected, recorded at the moment of physical sampling in ISO 8601-like form such as 2026-05-14T08:30:00. Use local site time or UTC consistently across the dataset.

Categorical descriptor of the sampling time window for the air collection event. Record the approximate time context at collection, not the exact timestamp. Useful for comparing daytime and nighttime urban air samples.

Categorical description of the ambient weather condition at the time of air sample collection, recorded as a sample-level contextual attribute. Use the observed condition at the sampling point, not instrument readings.

Categorical descriptor of the surrounding urban land-use context at the sample location, such as traffic-dominated street, residential area, commercial district, park, or industrial zone. Record this at collection to support interpretation of airborne microbial diversity.

air_environment_capture.reasoning: For the Capture node air_environment_capture, I included only the measurement-session and instrument-configuration fields that are actively controlled or defined during the field sensing event: the sensor suite identity, its configuration, and the measured environmental variables (air temperature, relative humidity, and particulate matter). I excluded sample identity/provenance because that belongs to the urban_air_sample Entity node, and I excluded raw digital file properties because those belong to the ambient_conditions_signal Signal node. I also avoided downstream processing or interpretation fields. Since no already_generated fields were provided for this turn, I did not need to suppress duplicates, but I still kept the schema focused on capture-side information only.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the portable environmental sensor suite used for the field measurement event. Record the hardware vendor controlling the capture session, for example Vaisala or Thermo Fisher Scientific.

Model name or number of the portable environmental sensor suite used during the air environment capture session, for example HM70 or DustTrak DRX 8533. Record the configured instrument model at the measurement point.

Unique serial number of the sensor suite used for the capture event; use the number printed on the instrument, for example SN1234567. This identifies the exact hardware instance used for the field measurement.

Firmware version installed on the portable environmental sensor suite at the time of measurement, for example 3.2.1. Record at the capture session because firmware can affect calibration and output behavior.

Air temperature measured during the capture event, in degrees Celsius. Record the sensor reading at the sampling point; typical urban field values may range from about -20 to 50 C depending on season and location.
Relative humidity measured during the capture event, expressed as percent from 0 to 100. Record the live field reading at the sampling point, concurrent with air sampling.

Particulate matter concentration measured during the capture event, in micrograms per cubic meter. Record the configured PM metric used by the sensor (for example PM2.5 or PM10, as specified elsewhere in the capture protocol) at the time of sampling; typical urban values may range from 0 to several hundred ug/m3.
Categorical designation of which particulate matter fraction was captured by the instrument during the measurement event. Record the active PM metric corresponding to the concentration value.

Categorical indicator of whether the environmental measurement session completed normally and produced usable readings. Use this at the capture level to summarize obvious session issues such as sensor fault or incomplete acquisition, not file-level quality.

ambient_conditions_signal.reasoning: For the Signal node ambient_conditions_signal, I included only raw data artefact fields: file identity, storage/format, size, dimensionality, and technical quality indicators for the digital environmental readings produced by the capture event. I excluded the actual temperature, humidity, and particulate matter values because those are the capture-side measurements, and I excluded any sensor manufacturer/model information because that belongs to the Capture node. I also avoided any interpretation or processing fields because this node is the raw signal, not a derivative. No already_generated fields were supplied here, so I did not need to suppress overlap, but I kept the schema strictly within signal/file territory.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw digital file containing the ambient condition readings produced by the field capture system, for example siteA_ambient_2026-05-14.csv. Record the file identity of the raw signal artefact, not the sample or sensor identifier.

Storage location or URI of the raw ambient conditions data file, for example s3://bucket/path/file.csv or /data/raw/ambient/file.csv. Record where the raw signal is stored for access and reproducibility.

Technical file format of the raw ambient condition signal, recorded at the file level, for example csv, json, txt, or binary. This describes how the capture output is encoded, not the content of the environmental measurements.
Size of the raw ambient conditions signal file in bytes, measured after acquisition and before processing. Typical values depend on sampling duration and device logging frequency.

Number of raw measurement records contained in the ambient conditions signal file. Record this at the file level to describe the amount of captured sensor output, typically spanning from tens to many thousands of rows.

Logging frequency of the raw ambient condition signal in hertz, describing how often the sensor output was written to the file during capture. Typical values may range from 0.1 to 10 Hz depending on the field protocol.

Categorical technical quality indicator for the raw ambient conditions file, summarizing whether the signal is complete and readable. Use this for file-level issues such as truncation, corruption, or missing blocks.

nucleic_acid_extraction.reasoning: For the Process node nucleic_acid_extraction, I included only protocol and reagent-level information describing how the extraction transformation was performed, plus a process-level outcome/quality indicator. I excluded source sample identity and origin because those belong to the Entity node urban_air_sample, and I excluded the extracted nucleic acid material’s intrinsic properties because those belong to the downstream Entity node extracted_nucleic_acids. I also avoided any sequencing-related parameters or file properties because they are outside this process’s semantic territory. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so I did not need to suppress duplicates, but I kept the schema strictly about the extraction workflow and not its inputs or outputs.

md_schema.descr: Name or standardized label of the nucleic acid extraction protocol applied to the collected airborne material, for example bead_beating_kit_v2 or phenol_chloroform_standard. Record the protocol used at the start of the extraction process.
Manufacturer of the extraction kit or reagent system used during nucleic acid extraction, for example Qiagen or Thermo Fisher Scientific. Record the reagent provider associated with the process.
Kit or reagent set model/version used for the extraction process, for example DNeasy PowerSoil Pro or MagMAX Viral/Pathogen. Record the exact kit formulation used for this process step.

Mass of collected airborne material subjected to extraction, in milligrams. Record the input amount at the beginning of the extraction process; typical values may range from sub-mg to tens of mg depending on collection efficiency.
Duration of the lysis step during nucleic acid extraction, in minutes. Record the actual process time used to disrupt cells and release nucleic acids, typically ranging from 5 to 120 minutes.

Temperature used during any extraction incubation or lysis incubation step, in degrees Celsius. Record the controlled process temperature, typically ranging from room temperature to about 65 C depending on the protocol.
Final elution volume used to recover nucleic acids from the extraction, in microliters. Record the process parameter at the end of extraction; common values may range from 20 to 100 uL.

Total nucleic acid yield obtained from the extraction process, in nanograms. Record this as a process-level outcome metric after extraction completion; typical yields may vary widely from below 1 ng to several hundred ng.

Categorical outcome indicator summarizing whether the extraction process completed successfully and produced usable nucleic acids. Use this process-level status to capture failures or low-yield extractions.

extracted_nucleic_acids.reasoning: For the Entity node extracted_nucleic_acids, I included only intrinsic properties of the purified nucleic acid material itself: identifier, material type, concentration, total amount, purity, integrity, fragment size, and storage conditions. I excluded extraction protocol details because those belong to the nucleic_acid_extraction Process node, and I excluded sequencing instrument or library preparation settings because those belong downstream. I also avoided sample-origin fields that duplicate the upstream urban_air_sample node. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so I did not have to suppress overlap with prior schema items, but I kept the schema focused on the physical/chemical state of the extracted material only.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the extracted nucleic acid material aliquot; use a stable string format such as NA-001 or extract_siteA_01. Assign this at the point the purified material is created and tracked for downstream sequencing.

Categorical type of extracted nucleic acid material present in the aliquot, recorded as the intrinsic composition of the extract. Use the dominant or intended material type at the time of downstream preparation.

Concentration of the extracted nucleic acid material, in nanograms per microliter, measured after purification and before library preparation. Typical values may range from below 1 ng/uL to hundreds of ng/uL depending on sample quality.

Total mass of nucleic acid recovered in the extracted aliquot, in nanograms. Record this after extraction completion and before sequencing preparation; typical values may range from sub-ng to several hundred ng.
Spectrophotometric purity ratio A260/A280 measured on the extracted nucleic acid aliquot after purification. Typical values for clean nucleic acids are around 1.8 for DNA and around 2.0 for RNA.

Integrity or quality score for the extracted nucleic acid material, measured after purification and before sequencing. Use the platform-specific integrity metric, for example RIN or DIN, with the numeric score recorded as provided by the instrument.

Approximate dominant fragment size of the extracted nucleic acids, in base pairs, measured after purification if applicable. Record the size representative of the extract; typical values may range from a few hundred bp to tens of thousands of bp depending on sample and extraction method.

Temperature at which the extracted nucleic acid aliquot is stored after purification and before downstream sequencing, in degrees Celsius. Record the storage condition for the material itself, for example -80 for long-term frozen storage.

Buffer or solution in which the extracted nucleic acids are stored or resuspended after purification, for example nuclease_free_water or elution_buffer. Record the immediate storage medium for the material.

Categorical intrinsic quality indicator summarizing whether the extracted nucleic acid material is suitable for downstream sequencing. Use this at the entity level to capture material state such as degradation or contamination.

metagenomic_sequencing_capture.reasoning: For the Capture node metagenomic_sequencing_capture, I included only the instrument and measurement-session fields that define how the sequencing run was configured: sequencer manufacturer/model/serial, chemistry, read configuration, run cycle settings, loading input, and run-level quality controls. I excluded extracted nucleic acid intrinsic properties because those belong to the extracted_nucleic_acids Entity node, and I excluded the raw read file properties because those belong to the raw_metagenomic_reads Signal node. I also avoided computational processing fields because those are downstream Process nodes. No already_generated fields were provided here, so I did not need to suppress overlap, but I kept the schema strictly in capture/instrument territory.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for the metagenomic capture session. Record the hardware vendor controlling the run, for example Illumina or Oxford Nanopore Technologies.
Sequencing instrument model used for the capture event, for example NovaSeq 6000, MiSeq, or MinION. Record the exact platform model configured for the run.
Serial number of the sequencing instrument used during the run; use the hardware serial printed on the instrument, for example SN987654. This identifies the exact sequencer instance used for capture.

Sequencing chemistry or kit version used on the instrument during the run, for example v2, v3, or 2x150 paired-end chemistry. Record the chemistry at the capture session because it determines read generation behavior.

Configured read length in base pairs for the sequencing run, measured as the intended output read size at the instrument settings stage. Typical values may range from 50 to 3000 bp depending on platform.
Whether the sequencing capture session was configured to generate paired-end reads. Record this instrument setting at run setup, before raw data generation.
Type of flow cell or consumable used for the sequencing capture session, for example S2, SP, or flow cell version identifiers. Record the active sequencing consumable used in the instrument.

Total duration of the sequencing run on the instrument, in hours. Record the actual capture session duration from start to completion; typical runs may last from a few hours to several days depending on platform.

Amount of extracted nucleic acid loaded into the sequencing instrument for the run, in nanograms. Record the input mass at capture setup; typical values may range from sub-ng to hundreds of ng depending on library requirements.
Categorical run-level quality indicator summarizing whether the sequencing capture session completed successfully and generated usable raw reads. Use this to capture gross instrument or run failures.

raw_metagenomic_reads.reasoning: I fixed the schema by removing fields that collide with already_generated across the DAG: file_format, file_size_bytes, and read_length_bp. I kept the remaining fields within the raw Signal territory for raw_metagenomic_reads: file identity/storage, read count, paired-end status, mean quality, adapter contamination, and lane provenance. I did not add any upstream capture settings, processing parameters, or derivative interpretations, and I preserved the raw-file focus without duplicating fields already used elsewhere in the workflow.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw sequencing file containing metagenomic reads, for example sampleA_R1.fastq.gz or run42.bam. Record the file identity of the raw signal artefact produced by the sequencer.

Storage location or URI for the raw metagenomic reads file, for example s3://bucket/raw/sampleA.fastq.gz or /data/raw_reads/run42.fq.gz. Record where the raw sequencing signal is stored for access and reanalysis.
Total number of sequencing reads contained in the raw metagenomic reads file. Record this as the raw output count prior to filtering or trimming; typical values may range from thousands to billions.
Whether the raw metagenomic reads are organized as paired-end data. Record the structure of the raw signal file, not the capture instrument setting.

Average base-call quality score across the raw metagenomic reads, computed from the raw file but reported here as a technical quality summary of the unprocessed signal. Typical values depend on platform and run quality.
Categorical technical flag indicating whether adapter contamination is present in the raw read file. Use this file-level indicator to summarize obvious raw signal contamination before processing.

Sequencing lane or partition identifier associated with the raw reads when applicable, for example lane1 or laneA. Record this file-level provenance to distinguish raw data segments from the same run.

read_processing.reasoning: For the Process node read_processing, I included only computational workflow parameters and processing outcomes that describe how raw sequencing reads were transformed into a cleaned signal. I excluded raw file properties because those belong to the raw_metagenomic_reads Signal node, and I excluded taxonomic or abundance outputs because those belong downstream to taxonomic_profiling and the derivative node. I also avoided repeating already_generated fields by not using file_format, file_size_bytes, or read_length_bp, which were flagged as collisions across DAG steps. The schema therefore focuses on the software workflow, trimming/filtering settings, and process-level quality indicators needed to reproduce the read processing step.

md_schema.descr: Name of the computational software or pipeline used to process raw sequencing reads, for example fastp or custom_qc_pipeline. Record the software used for the read-processing step only.
Version of the read-processing software or pipeline, for example 0.23.4 or v1.0. Record the exact version used so the filtering and trimming behavior can be reproduced.
Repository or source location of the read-processing software, for example a GitHub URL or container registry reference. Record this to identify the implementation used for the computational process.
Tool or algorithm used specifically to trim adapter sequence from raw reads during processing, for example cutadapt or built-in fastp trimming. Record the method used at the processing step.

Minimum Phred quality threshold applied during read filtering or trimming, measured on the standard Phred scale. Typical values may range from 10 to 35 depending on the desired stringency; record the threshold used at processing time.
Minimum read length retained after filtering and trimming, in base pairs. Record the cutoff applied during processing; typical thresholds may range from 30 to 100 bp depending on protocol.
Whether host or non-microbial sequence removal was performed during read processing. Record this process setting as a yes/no choice for the computational cleanup stage.

Number of reads retained after computational filtering and trimming. Record this process-level outcome after read processing completes; it summarizes the output quantity without describing the output file itself.

Percentage of raw reads retained after read processing, calculated as retained reads divided by input reads times 100. Record this as a process-quality indicator for the cleanup step; typical values may range from a small fraction to nearly 100 depending on stringency.

Categorical indicator summarizing whether the read-processing step completed successfully and produced reads suitable for downstream profiling. Use this to capture gross process-level problems such as excessive loss or pipeline failure.

processed_metagenomic_reads.reasoning: For the Signal node processed_metagenomic_reads, I kept the schema in raw/processed file territory and corrected the collision by removing the already-used field id processed_read_count. I preserved file identity, storage, format, size, technical quality, and status fields because these describe the processed artefact itself. I excluded process parameters from read_processing and avoided biological interpretation or downstream profiling outputs. I also kept clear of previously colliding generic field names like file_format, file_size_bytes, and read_length_bp by using processed-specific names.

md_schema.descr: Name of the quality-filtered metagenomic reads file, for example sampleA_trimmed.fastq.gz. Record the file identity of the processed signal artefact produced by read processing.

Storage location or URI of the processed metagenomic reads file, for example s3://bucket/processed/sampleA_trimmed.fastq.gz or /data/processed_reads/sampleA.fq.gz. Record where the cleaned signal is stored for downstream profiling.

Technical file format of the processed metagenomic reads, recorded at the file level, for example fastq, fasta, bam, or cram. This describes the encoding of the cleaned signal, not the processing parameters.

Size of the processed metagenomic reads file in bytes, measured after cleaning and before downstream profiling. Typical values may range from megabytes to hundreds of gigabytes depending on sequencing depth and filtering.

Average base-call quality score across the processed metagenomic reads, summarized at the file level after filtering and trimming. Record this as a technical quality metric for the cleaned signal; typical values are usually higher than in the raw file.
Whether duplicate reads were removed during read processing and are absent from the processed file. Record this file-level property if deduplication was part of the cleanup workflow.

Categorical flag indicating the apparent level of residual contamination in the processed read file after cleaning. Use this as a technical summary of the processed signal quality, not as a biological interpretation.

Categorical indicator of whether the processed metagenomic reads file was successfully generated and is ready for taxonomic profiling. Use this as a file-level usability status for the cleaned signal.

taxonomic_profiling.reasoning: For the Process node taxonomic_profiling, I included only computational profiling parameters and process-level outputs that describe how processed reads were assigned to taxa. I excluded raw and processed read file properties because those belong to the Signal nodes, and I excluded downstream abundance table properties because those belong to the microbial_abundance_matrix Derivative node. I also avoided previously generated field names and their near-equivalents, including processed_read_count, to prevent collisions across DAG steps. The schema focuses on the profiling software, classification database, assignment thresholds, and run-level assignment statistics needed to reproduce the taxonomic profiling step.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to assign processed metagenomic reads to microbial taxa, for example kraken2, metaphlan, or a custom profiler. Record the computational tool used for the profiling process.
Version of the taxonomic profiling software or pipeline, for example 2.1.2 or v1.0. Record the exact version used so the assignment behavior can be reproduced.

Name of the reference taxonomy database used for read assignment, for example GTDB, SILVA, or Kraken standard database. Record the database used at the profiling step, not the downstream result table.
Version or release date of the reference database used for taxonomic profiling, for example 2024-01 or release_220. Record the exact database version to support reproducibility.

Minimum confidence or score threshold applied when assigning processed reads to taxa, measured on the profiler's native scale. Typical values depend on the software and may range from 0 to 1 or from low to high scores; record the threshold used at profiling time.

Minimum relative abundance threshold applied during taxonomic profiling or post-assignment filtering, expressed as percent. Typical values may range from 0.01 to 1 percent depending on reporting stringency.

Percentage of processed reads successfully assigned to at least one taxon by the profiling software. Record this as a process-level outcome after profiling completes; it summarizes classification coverage without describing the output abundance table.

Percentage of processed reads that could not be confidently assigned to any taxon during profiling. Record this as a process-level indicator of unclassified signal remaining after taxonomic assignment.

Categorical process-level indicator summarizing whether the taxonomic profiling step completed successfully and produced usable taxonomic assignments. Use this to capture gross profiling failures or poor assignment performance.

microbial_abundance_matrix.reasoning: For the Derivative node microbial_abundance_matrix, I included only computed-result fields that describe the abundance table itself: matrix identity, transformation/normalization method, dimensions, taxa resolution, sparsity, and summary quality indicators. I excluded taxonomic profiling software and database parameters because those belong to the taxonomic_profiling Process node, and I excluded the underlying reads because those are upstream Signal nodes. I also avoided already-generated field names and near-equivalents, including processed_read_count and other signal/process terms, so the schema stays within the derived table territory and does not collide across DAG steps.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed microbial abundance matrix; use a stable string format such as abund_matrix_001 or taxprof_run12_matrix. Assign this to the derived table produced by the profiling step.
Storage or serialization format of the abundance matrix, for example csv, tsv, parquet, or hdf5. Record the format of the computed table itself, not the raw sequencing file format.

Taxonomic rank represented by the rows or columns of the abundance matrix, for example species, genus, family, or otu. Record the resolution of the computed table used to summarize microbial community composition.

Number of unique taxa represented in the abundance matrix, counted after profiling and any filtering. Typical values may range from a few dozen to many thousands depending on sequencing depth and taxonomic resolution.

Number of urban air samples represented in the abundance matrix, measured as the number of sample columns or rows in the derived table depending on orientation. Record this as the matrix dimension relevant to downstream analysis.

Method used to normalize or transform taxon counts in the abundance matrix, for example relative_abundance, rarefaction, clr, or none. Record the transformation applied to the computed table before analysis.

Percentage of matrix entries that are zero or absent in the computed abundance table. Record this derived table property as a summary of matrix sparsity; typical values may be high for metagenomic datasets.

Average abundance value across all taxa entries in the matrix, measured on the chosen normalized scale. Record this as a table-level summary statistic of the derived data; typical values depend on normalization.

Categorical indicator summarizing whether the derived abundance matrix is internally consistent and usable for downstream association analysis. Use this to capture issues such as extreme sparsity, missing samples, or failed normalization.

joint_environmental_analysis.reasoning: For the Process node joint_environmental_analysis, I included only analysis-level parameters and output quality indicators that describe how the microbial abundance matrix was integrated with ambient environmental data. I excluded the ambient measurements themselves because those belong to the air_environment_capture Capture node and ambient_conditions_signal Signal node, and I excluded the abundance matrix properties because those belong to the microbial_abundance_matrix Derivative node. I also avoided duplicating software fields from earlier computational steps by using analysis-specific names and focusing on statistical model settings, covariate handling, and process-level fit/effect summaries. No already_generated fields were supplied here, so there was no need to suppress direct collisions, but the schema remains confined to the joint analysis process.

md_schema.descr: Name of the statistical or computational software used for the joint environmental analysis, for example R, Python, or statsmodels-based custom code. Record the software used to integrate microbial and environmental data.
Version of the statistical analysis software or pipeline, for example 4.3.1 or 2.1. Record the exact version used so the analysis can be reproduced.
Repository, package source, or code location for the joint environmental analysis workflow, for example a GitHub URL or package name. Record this to identify the implementation used for the analysis.

Type of statistical model used to assess associations between microbial abundance and environmental variables, for example linear_model, mixed_effects_model, correlation_analysis, or multivariate_regression. Record the model family used at the analysis step.

Number of covariates included in the joint environmental model beyond microbial abundance and the measured environmental variables, counted at model specification time. Typical values may range from 0 upward depending on the analysis design.
Method used to correct for multiple comparisons in the joint analysis, for example fdr, bonferroni, or none. Record the correction applied when evaluating many taxa or associations.

Threshold used to declare a microbial-environment association significant, measured on the relevant statistical scale such as p-value or adjusted p-value. Typical values may range from 0.001 to 0.1 depending on the study design; record the threshold used at analysis time.

Summary effect size metric reported by the joint analysis, for example a correlation coefficient or standardized regression coefficient. Record the analysis-level summary statistic used to describe association strength.

Categorical indicator summarizing whether the joint environmental analysis completed successfully and produced interpretable association results. Use this to capture model convergence issues, insufficient power, or other analysis-level problems.

urban_air_association_results.reasoning: For the Derivative node urban_air_association_results, I included only computed result fields that summarize the outputs of the joint environmental analysis: result identifier, result format, statistical summary type, number of tested associations, significance counts, effect-size summaries, top-hit summaries, and result quality. I excluded the upstream environmental measurements, abundance matrix properties, and analysis software parameters because those belong to Capture, Derivative, or Process nodes earlier in the DAG. I also avoided previously generated field names and their close equivalents, including file_format, file_size_bytes, read_length_bp, processed_read_count, and other signal/process terms, to prevent collisions across DAG steps. The schema is therefore focused on the final association-result artefact only.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed urban air association results object; use a stable string format such as assoc_results_001 or joint_env_run3_results. Assign this to the final derived results artefact produced by the joint environmental analysis.

Storage or serialization format of the association results, for example csv, tsv, json, parquet, or html. Record the format of the computed result artefact itself, not the upstream raw or processed data files.

Type of statistical summary used in the association results, for example correlation, regression_coefficient, odds_ratio, p_value, or adjusted_p_value. Record the principal numeric summary reported by the final analysis output.

Number of microbial-environment associations evaluated in the final results set, counted across taxa, environmental variables, and model terms. Typical values may range from a few to many thousands depending on the analysis design.
Number of associations in the final results that met the study's significance threshold after correction. Record this as a result-level summary of the computed output.

Effect size of the strongest or most representative association reported in the final results, measured on the scale used by the analysis such as correlation coefficient or standardized regression coefficient. Typical values depend on model type and interpretation scale.
P-value corresponding to the top association reported in the final results, recorded on the statistical scale used by the analysis. Use this to summarize the strongest result in the derived output.
Primary environmental factor highlighted in the final association results, for example temperature, humidity, or particulate matter. Record the most relevant factor emphasized in the computed output.

Categorical indicator summarizing whether the final association results are complete, interpretable, and ready for reporting. Use this for result-level issues such as failed models, missing summary tables, or inconsistent outputs.
